chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Abu Abdillah al-Razi, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Mandal, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj and Dawud ibn Farqad (both) from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), they said:

We asked him about a man who has wealth for orphans, and he does not give it to them until they die; then their heir and their agent come to him, and he makes a settlement with him to take some [of the wealth] and leave some, and to acquit him from what he would have been acquitted of. He [the Imam] said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.يُبْرِئَهُ: he acquits him / releases him from liability

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling for a guardian who withholds an orphan's wealth until the orphan dies?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *sulh* (amicable settlement) in guardianship, allowing a guardian to buy out his liability for orphan wealth by paying a portion agreed upon by the heir or agent. It highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence for resolving disputes over delayed distribution of orphan assets, ensuring the guardian is released from further claims once the settlement is accepted.
